statement: Conduction-associated cardiomyocyte populations (including ncCM-IFT-like, ncCM-AVC-like, and vCM-His-Purkinje) form spatially segregated, strongly self-associated microdomains that are modestly enriched for neuronal neighbors compared with working ventricular cardiomyocytes and exhibit a shared developmental and conduction-related gene program that is distinct from the surrounding ventricular myocardium.
mechanism: Rare-but-tight analysis shows ncCM-IFT-like and ncCM-AVC-like cardiomyocytes are highly spatially concentrated and have enriched nearest neighbors from specific non-cardiomyocyte types (e.g. aFibro, adFibro, Neuronal, BEC), and pairwise co-localization reveals strong self-association of vCM-His-Purkinje, suggesting conduction-like niches with distinctive immediate environments.
test_plan: 1) Define a 'conduction-like' group consisting of cells with Populations labels in ['ncCM-IFT-like', 'ncCM-AVC-like', 'vCM-His-Purkinje'] and a 'working-vCM' group including major ventricular cardiomyocyte labels such as ['vCM-LV-Compact', 'vCM-LV-Trabecular', 'vCM-RV-Compact', 'vCM-Proliferating']. 2) Using the precomputed k=20 neighbor indices on spatial coordinates, compute for each conduction-like and working-vCM cell the fraction of neighbors belonging to fibroblast (aFibro, vFibro, adFibro), endothelial (BEC, VEC, vEndocardial), and Neuronal populations. Compare neighbor-type distributions between conduction-like and working-vCM groups using contingency tables and effect sizes (e.g. differences in mean neighbor fractions). 3) Perform differential expression between conduction-like and working-vCM cells using the AnnData expression matrix to rank genes by log-fold-change, and then summarize whether conduction-like cells show coherent upregulation of a multi-gene program (e.g. ion-channel, gap-junction, or guidance-related genes present in the panel) relative to working-vCM cells.
predicted_outcome: If the hypothesis holds, conduction-like cardiomyocytes will show higher fractions of fibroblast, endothelial, and neuronal neighbors than working-vCM cells, with neighbor-type differences that are substantially larger than sampling noise, and differential expression will reveal a coherent set of ≥5 genes jointly upregulated in conduction-like cells compared to working-vCM cells. The hypothesis would be weakened or falsified if neighbor-type compositions are similar between conduction-like and working-vCM groups and if no clear multi-gene expression program distinguishes conduction-like from working-vCM cells.
narrowing_notes: Tested neighbor composition for conduction-like cardiomyocytes (ncCM-IFT-like, ncCM-AVC-like, vCM-His-Purkinje; n=9,748) versus working ventricular cardiomyocytes (vCM-LV-Compact, vCM-LV-Trabecular, vCM-RV-Compact, vCM-Proliferating; n=73,963) using k=20 spatial nearest neighbors. Conduction-like cells had slightly lower mean fractions of fibroblast neighbors (0.101 vs 0.121; Mann–Whitney p≈2×10⁻²⁴⁷) and endothelial neighbors (0.083 vs 0.107; p<10⁻³⁰⁰) than working ventricular cells, contradicting the prediction of increased fibroblast/endothelial contact. In contrast, conduction-like cells showed a higher neuronal neighbor fraction (0.010 vs ≈0.000; p<10⁻³⁰⁰), consistent with modest neuronal enrichment. Differential expression between conduction-like and working ventricular cardiomyocytes revealed a strong, coherent gene program: 72 of 238 genes had log₂ fold-change>0.5 and 36>1.0, with top upregulated genes including BMP2, ISL1, NR2F1, TBX3, RSPO3, IRX1, IRX2, JAG1, TRPM3, and FBLN2. Together with the rare-but-tight and pairwise co-localization results (very high self-edge enrichment for conduction-related labels), this supports spatially segregated conduction microdomains with a distinct developmental/conduction transcriptional program, but does not support broad enrichment for fibroblast or endothelial neighbors. The hypothesis was therefore narrowed to emphasize self-association, neuronal enrichment, and the shared gene program rather than generalized stromal enrichment.

statement: Lymphatic endothelial cells, adipogenic fibroblasts, and epicardial- or epicardial-derived cells form a spatially co-localized niche in which adipogenic fibroblasts display a transcriptional program distinct from ventricular fibroblasts, characterized by coordinated upregulation of multiple extracellular-matrix, remodeling-associated, and guidance- or signaling-related genes present in the panel, with additional modulation of this program in adipogenic fibroblasts that reside directly within the niche.
mechanism: Rare-but-tight analysis indicates adFibro and LEC are both highly concentrated and that adFibro cells have strongly enriched LEC, WBC, and Epicardial neighbors, while LEC cells show enriched neighbors including adFibro and EPDC. Pairwise co-localization further shows highly enriched adFibro→adFibro and adFibro→LEC neighbor edges, suggesting a stable lymphatic–fibroblast–epicardial microenvironment with potentially distinct fibroblast gene regulation.
test_plan: 1) Define an 'adFibro-niche' set consisting of adFibro cells and their direct neighbors that are LEC, Epicardial, or EPDC, and a comparison set of ventricular fibroblasts (vFibro) located outside this niche (e.g. vFibro cells whose k=20 neighbors include no LEC, Epicardial, or EPDC). 2) Quantify spatial co-localization by computing observed vs expected neighbor-type frequencies for adFibro↔LEC, adFibro↔Epicardial, and adFibro↔EPDC pairs and compare them to vFibro↔LEC/Epicardial/EPDC pairs. 3) Perform differential expression between adFibro cells inside the niche and vFibro cells, ranking genes by log-fold-change, and identify multi-gene sets corresponding to extracellular matrix components or inflammatory mediators (e.g. families such as collagens, matrix metalloproteinases, or chemokines within the available panel). 4) Optionally, compare adFibro inside the niche to any adFibro cells that lack LEC/Epicardial neighbors to test whether niche proximity is associated with stronger activation of the same gene program.
predicted_outcome: If the hypothesis is correct, adFibro cells will show markedly higher frequencies of LEC, Epicardial, and EPDC neighbors than vFibro cells, and adFibro inside the niche will display a coherent set of ≥5 genes with higher expression than vFibro (and than adFibro outside the niche if present), including multiple extracellular-matrix or remodeling-related genes from the panel. The hypothesis would be undermined if neighbor compositions of adFibro and vFibro are similar with little enrichment for LEC or Epicardial neighbors, or if differential expression reveals no clear multi-gene program distinguishing adFibro from vFibro.
narrowing_notes: Neighbor analysis compared adipogenic fibroblasts (adFibro; n=1,562) to ventricular fibroblasts (vFibro; n=16,624) using k=20 spatial neighbors. adFibro cells had much higher mean fractions of lymphatic endothelial neighbors (LEC: 0.109 vs 0.001), epicardial neighbors (Epicardial: 0.043 vs 0.001), and EPDC neighbors (0.055 vs 0.013), and a combined Any(LEC/Epicardial/EPDC) neighbor fraction of 0.208 vs 0.015 in vFibro (all Mann–Whitney p<10⁻²⁷⁰). At the cell level, 46.1% of adFibro cells had at least one LEC neighbor, 32.2% at least one Epicardial neighbor, 36.2% at least one EPDC neighbor, and 62.7% had at least one of these niche neighbors, compared with 1.5%, 1.1%, 7.6%, and 8.0% respectively for vFibro, indicating a tightly co-localized lymphatic–fibroblast–epicardial niche. Differential expression between adFibro and vFibro showed a strong program: 99 of 238 genes had log₂ fold-change>0.5 and 54>1.0, with top upregulated genes including PIEZO2, OSR1, MFAP5, NR2F1, MYH11, CRABP2, NPR3, FNDC1, LYVE1, FBLN5, HOXA5, F13A1, and COL14A1, encompassing extracellular-matrix components and remodeling- or signaling-associated factors. Within adFibro, cells in the niche (≥1 LEC/Epicardial/EPDC neighbor; n=979) versus outside (n=583) showed additional transcriptional differences, with 40 genes having log₂ fold-change>0.5 and 8>1.0; top niche-enriched genes included CLDN5, PENK, NKD2, LYVE1, WT1, NRP2, F13A1, and GJA1, suggesting further modulation of the program linked to direct niche contact. These results support the existence of a lymphatic–adipogenic fibroblast–epicardial niche and a distinct, niche-sensitive adFibro gene program relative to vFibro.
